{"code": "from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Create a copy for modeling
df_model = df.copy()

# One-hot encode customer_segment
df_model = pd.get_dummies(df_model, columns=['customer_segment'], drop_first=True)

# Create age_group and one-hot encode it
df_model['age_group'] = pd.cut(df_model['customer_age'], bins=[0, 30, 50, 100], labels=['Young', 'Middle-aged', 'Old'])
df_model = pd.get_dummies(df_model, columns=['age_group'], drop_first=True)

# Define features and target
X = df_model[['channel', 'customer_segment_loyal', 'customer_segment_new', 'age_group_Middle-aged', 'age_group_Old']]
# We need to encode 'channel' as a dummy variable
X = pd.get_dummies(X, columns=['channel'], drop_first=True)

# Use 'email' as the reference group, so 'paid_search' will be the dummy
y = df_model['converted']

# Fit logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
model.fit(X, y)

# Predictions and coefficients
# The coefficient for 'channel_paid_search' is the log-odds difference
coef_paid_search = model.coef_[0][0]  # coefficient for paid_search vs email

# Convert log-odds to probability difference using average marginal effect
# We can compute the average treatment effect on the probability scale
# Use the mean of the predicted probabilities under each treatment
X_email = X.copy()
X_email['channel_paid_search'] = 0  # email group
X_paid_search = X.copy()
X_paid_search['channel_paid_search'] = 1  # paid_search group

# Predict probabilities
pred_email = model.predict_proba(X_email)[:, 1]
pred_paid_search = model.predict_proba(X_paid_search)[:, 1]

# Average treatment effect on probability
ate = pred_paid_search.mean() - pred_email.mean()

# But we want email minus paid_search
ate_difference = -ate  # because we are computing email - paid_search

ate_difference"}
